title: machine: delete stale API socket before starting the proxy on Windows
body:
# machine/windows: remove stale API socket before starting the API forwarder

Fixes #29971

If the Windows host shuts down or restarts with a machine running, `win-sshproxy` leaves the API socket file behind. On the next `podman machine start` the proxy can't listen and exits, so the API is unavailable. WSL starts with no pipe, and Hyper-V fails with exit 125 (`machine is not listening on ssh port`).

This is a regression from gvisor-tap-vsock v0.9.0 (containers/gvisor-tap-vsock#718). That release dropped the `os.Remove(path)` before listen, and Windows shutdown never reaches the listener's Close.

## Fix

`cleanupStaleHostForwarder` now runs the existing orphan proxy check (moved to `cleanupStaleProxyProcess`) and then deletes `mc.APISocket()`, ignoring not-exist. The deletion is safe for three reasons. It only happens after the orphan check passes, it runs under the machine lock (and the start lock on Hyper-V), and it applies to both WSL and Hyper-V through `startNetworking`.

## Testing

A new e2e test (`start_windows_test.go`) kills the proxy, checks the socket was left behind, stops and starts the machine, then pings the API over the pipe. On WSL it fails on main `1644490` and passes with this change. Manual kill → stop → start runs on WSL and Hyper-V both bring the pipe back with this change. `make .validatepr` passes.

## Open questions

- The test uses `taskkill /IM`, which kills every proxy on the host. Should it use a PID-based kill instead?
- If deleting the socket fails, should `start` fail or only warn?
- @l0rd mentioned working on a fix. I'm happy to close this one if theirs covers more.
